glaucoma.title: Topical Tacrolimus in Ocular Disease: A Narrative Review of Mechanism of Action and Therapeutic Applications.
glaucoma.summary: Topical tacrolimus is an effective steroid-sparing immunomodulator for a broad spectrum of T-cell-mediated ocular disease, with a favorable safety profile notable for the absence of steroid-related rises in intraocular pressure or cataractogenesis. Standardized formulations and prospective comparative trials remain priorities.
glaucoma.abstract: PURPOSE: Immune-mediated inflammatory disorders of the ocular surface and anterior segment frequently require sustained immunosuppression, yet prolonged topical corticosteroid use carries the risk of glaucoma, cataract, and infection. Tacrolimus, a macrolide calcineurin inhibitor, has emerged as a steroid-sparing alternative for T-cell-mediated ocular disease. This review summarizes the mechanism of action, ocular pharmacology, clinical applications, and safety profile of topical tacrolimus. METHODS: Narrative synthesis of the peer-reviewed literature. RESULTS: Tacrolimus binds the immunophilin FK506-binding protein 12; the resulting complex inhibits the phosphatase calcineurin, preventing dephosphorylation and nuclear translocation of the nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFAT) and thereby suppressing transcription of interleukin-2 and a broad program of pro-inflammatory cytokines. glaucoma.summary: INTRODUCTION: Secondary glaucoma is a significant cause of visual morbidity and present a major challenge to ophthalmologists. Given their varied aetiological profile across regions, understanding the current spectrum is essential for early detection, timely diagnosis, and prompt management to prevent irreversible vision loss. …
glaucoma.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Secondary glaucoma is a significant cause of visual morbidity and present a major challenge to ophthalmologists. Given their varied aetiological profile across regions, understanding the current spectrum is essential for early detection, timely diagnosis, and prompt management to prevent irreversible vision loss. OBJECTIVE: To determine the clinical profile and aetiological pattern of secondary glaucoma in a tertiary eye care centre in Southern India. METHODOLOGY: This hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at a tertiary eye care centre in Southern India from 2023 December to 2024 May. Consecutive sampling technique was utilised and ethical approval was taken. glaucoma.abstract: Glaucoma is an irreversible progressive optic neuropathy, for which the major proven treatment is to lower the intraocular pressure (IOP). Five groups of IOP-lowering eye drops have varying mechanisms of action. Some drops, such as β-blockers and α-2 agonists, have potentially serious systemic side effects. Acetazolamide is the only available oral agent; it is effective at lowering IOP, but significant side effects relegate its use usually to refractory glaucoma. Two new eye drops, netarsudil and latanoprostene bunod, have recently been approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration. Both have novel IOP-lowering mechanisms and target the conventional aqueous outflow system. Selective laser trabeculoplasty is a gentle treatment that enhances conventional aqueous outflow. glaucoma.title: [MINIMALLY INVASIVE GLAUCOMA SURGERIES].
glaucoma.summary: The goal of all glaucoma surgery is to lower eye pressure to prevent or reduce damage to the optic nerve. Standard glaucoma surgeries - trabeculectomy, ExPRESS shunts and external tube-shunts like the Ahmed and Baerveldt valves - are major surgeries. …
glaucoma.abstract: The goal of all glaucoma surgery is to lower eye pressure to prevent or reduce damage to the optic nerve. Standard glaucoma surgeries - trabeculectomy, ExPRESS shunts and external tube-shunts like the Ahmed and Baerveldt valves - are major surgeries. While they are very often effective at lowering eye pressure and preventing progression of glaucoma, they have a long list of potential complications. Minimal invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) is a group of operations that have been developed in recent years to reduce some of the complications of most standard glaucoma surgeries. MIGS procedures work by using microscopic-sized equipment and tiny incisions. The purpose of this study is to review the available MIGS currently in use, their benefits and limitations.

glaucoma.abstract: The childhood glaucomas represent of variety of glaucoma subtypes that can cause serious and permanent visual damage. Early detection and treatment of infantile glaucoma is essential to preserve vision. The clinical signs and symptoms of infantile glaucoma are recognizable by nonophthalmologists but may be confused with other common clinical entities. Surgical and occasionally medical interventions can control raised intraocular pressure and thus prevent permanent glaucoma damage to the eye. Amblyopia is a common reason for permanent visual loss in this disease and needs to be treated aggressively as well.

glaucoma.summary: A technique called optical coherence tomography (OCT) has been developed for noninvasive cross-sectional imaging in biological systems. glaucoma.abstract: A technique called optical coherence tomography (OCT) has been developed for noninvasive cross-sectional imaging in biological systems. OCT uses low-coherence interferometry to produce a two-dimensional image of optical scattering from internal tissue microstructures in a way that is analogous to ultrasonic pulse-echo imaging. OCT has longitudinal and lateral spatial resolutions of a few micrometers and can detect reflected signals as small as approximately 10(-10) of the incident optical power. Tomographic imaging is demonstrated in vitro in the peripapillary area of the retina and in the coronary artery, two clinically relevant examples that are representative of transparent and turbid media, respectively.

glaucoma.title: Prostaglandins and inflammation
glaucoma.summary: Prostaglandins are lipid autacoids derived from arachidonic acid. They both sustain homeostatic functions and mediate pathogenic mechanisms, including the inflammatory response. …
glaucoma.abstract: Prostaglandins are lipid autacoids derived from arachidonic acid. They both sustain homeostatic functions and mediate pathogenic mechanisms, including the inflammatory response. They are generated from arachidonate by the action of cyclooxygenase isoenzymes, and their biosynthesis is blocked by nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs, including those selective for inhibition of cyclooxygenase-2. Despite the clinical efficacy of nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs, prostaglandins may function in both the promotion and resolution of inflammation. This review summarizes insights into the mechanisms of prostaglandin generation and the roles of individual mediators and their receptors in modulating the inflammatory response. Prostaglandin biology has potential clinical relevance for atherosclerosis, the response to vascular injury and aortic aneurysm.

At the same time, a reduction in the risk of macular fibrosis has been demonstrated, with its incidence decreasing from 39-100% in the "pre-antiangiogenic era" to 20.4-61.4% during anti-VEGF therapy. The main factors determining the risk of subretinal fibrosis are disease activity, timing of treatment initiation, treatment regimen and regularity, and type of drug. Fluctuations in retinal thickness and volatility of specific fluid compartments lead to an increase in the volume of subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM) and hinder complete restoration of ellipsoid zone integrity. This study presents the case of a 80-year-old man with a visual acuity of 20/800 in the right eye (OD). Multimodal imaging revealed perifoveolar telangiectasias, diffuse loss of the foveal reflex, and hyporeflective intraretinal cystoid spaces consistent with edema. The patient received 18 intravitreal injections of anti-VEGF agents (aflibercept, faricimab), with improvement to 20/40 and subsequent stabilization at 20/50 OD. The effects of different approaches on changes in morphological OCT biomarkers remain insufficiently studied. OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to compare the functional and anatomical outcomes of three perioperative strategies for DME treatment after cataract phacoemulsification. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 102 patients (102 eyes) with type 2 diabetes mellitus, DME, and cataract. Real-world evidence on faricimab within the Polish national drug program remains scarce. This study aimed to assess one-year clinical and treatment outcomes of faricimab for nAMD using real-world data from the Polish Therapeutic Program Monitoring System (SMPT). Methods: In this retrospective, non-randomized registry study, 322 patient-eye records treated with faricimab within the national drug program between January 2024 and April 2025 were analysed. Eligibility required at least 360 days between the first and last injections. This study quantified the incremental predictive value of month-1 imaging using a nested-model framework that mirrors the sequential clinical workflow. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included 124 treatment-naive nAMD eyes from 105 patients that completed three monthly anti-VEGF injections and had evaluable baseline, month-1, and month-3 imaging. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 50 eyes from 50 patients with previously treated DME and center-involving intraretinal and/or subretinal fluid at the time of switching. All eyes received four consecutive monthly intravitreal faricimab injections. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central macular thickness (CMT) were assessed through Month 4. retina.summary: Compared to aflibercept IVIs under a T&E regimen for bilateral nAMD, universal use of the PDP with 24-week refills is unlikely to be considered cost-effective in Norway. However, the PDP may be considered high-value for patients needing frequent IVI or facing long travel distances.
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: Standard ranibizumab anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) intravitreal injection (IVI) therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) may be alternatively delivered using the Port Delivery Platform (PDP), a drug delivery system surgically inserted into the eye that was re-approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in July 2024. Quantifying the added health benefits and cost consequences of new health interventions is required in various health systems. This study aims to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of universal and targeted use of the PDP with ranibizumab compared to treat-and-extend (T&E) aflibercept injections for patients with nAMD in Norway. METHODS: We compared the PDP with ranibizumab 100 mg/ml with fixed 24-week refill-exchanges (Q24W) to T&E IVI with vial split aflibercept 2 mg. We developed a probabilistic visual acuity-base

retina.title: Epivascular Glia and Macular Pigment Changes after Faricimab or Aflibercept during the Loading Phase in Diabetic Macular Edema: A Prospective Non-randomized Pilot Study.
retina.summary: EVG and traction- related outcomes were numerically more favorable with faricimab but were not statistically significant. Exploratory anatomical and MPOD differences require confirmation in larger randomized studies.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To explore short-term changes in epivascular glia (EVG), macular pigment optical density (MPOD), visual acuity, and retinal thickness after faricimab or aflibercept in treatment-naive eyes with center-involving diabetic macular edema (DME). METHODS: This prospective, non-randomized pilot study included 30 eyes with DME and EVG on en face optical coherence tomography. Fifteen eyes received three monthly injections of faricimab 6 mg and 15 received aflibercept 2 mg. The primary exploratory outcome was complete EVG regression after loading. Secondary outcomes included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central macular thickness (CMT), MPOD, fluid resolution, and resolution of traction-related abnormalities. retina.title: Switching to faricimab in anti-VEGF-refractory retinal vein occlusion: nine-month prospective real-world outcomes under a modified treat-and-extend regimen.
retina.summary: Switching to faricimab was associated with sustained anatomical improvement, modest functional benefit, and clinically meaningful interval extension. These findings support a response-guided modified T&E switch strategy without a conventional loading phase in treatment-intensive RVO.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate nine-month outcomes after switching to faricimab in anti-VEGF-refractory retinal vein occlusion (RVO) under a modified treat-and-extend (T&E) regimen. METHODS: In this prospective real-world study, 34 eyes of 34 patients with macular edema (ME) secondary to RVO were switched to faricimab. Eligibility required persistent center-involving intraretinal fluid (IRF) across the three most recent treatment visits, central subfield thickness (CST) ≥ 270 μm at switching, and ≥ 3 prior anti-VEGF injections with the three most recent intervals of 4-6 weeks and no ability to extend beyond six weeks. Treatment followed a modified T&E regimen with a single loading dose. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), CST, OCT biomarkers, and treatment intervals were evaluated through the fifth injection visit. retina.abstract: Reference aflibercept 2 mg (EYLEA; Regeneron/Bayer) remains a foundational therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, and macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion, supported by high binding affinity for vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A, VEGF-B, and placental growth factor, along with well-established durability and flexible dosing approaches. The retinal therapeutic landscape is evolving with the introduction of high-dose aflibercept 8 mg (EYLEA HD; Regeneron/Bayer), faricimab (VABYSMO; Roche), and biosimilar aflibercept such as YESAFILI (Biocon Biologics), each representing distinct pharmacologic and clinical strategies. retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study evaluated 12-month anatomical and functional outcomes of Faricimab in Italian patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). METHODS: 30 eyes from 30 participants who completed the 12-month follow-up were retrospectively analyzed at "Luigi Vanvitelli" University Eye Clinic (Naples) and "Rummo" Hospital Ophthalmology Unit (Benevento). All underwent best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). Patients were stratified by anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) treatment [naïve (N = 22); non-naïve (N = 8)], baseline macular neovascularization (MNV) type and fluid distribution. retina.summary: Since the publication in 2014 of the original EURETINA guidelines for the management of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), the treatment landscape for this prevalent and potentially devastating condition has evolved substantially. …
retina.abstract: Since the publication in 2014 of the original EURETINA guidelines for the management of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), the treatment landscape for this prevalent and potentially devastating condition has evolved substantially. Along with the introduction of new anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents and the release of biosimilar agents, anti-VEGF dosing strategies have been refined, and increasing amounts of clinical trial and real-world evidence are available to inform practice. To provide an updated European perspective on nAMD management, the EURETINA panel systematically reviewed European guidelines published since 2014 alongside recent randomized controlled trials and other relevant evidence. retina.title: Serum Ang-1, sFLT-1, and sST2 Profiles Distinguish Anti-VEGF Responders in Diabetic Macular Edema.
retina.summary: Ang-1, sFLT-1, and sST2 are closely associated with treatment response to anti-VEGF therapy in DME patients, highlighting their roles in vascular integrity, endogenous VEGF blockade, and inflammation regulation. Both the cytokines individual levels and their ratios serve as early indicators of the success of anti-VEGF treatment in DME. …
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: Diabetic macular edema (DME) remains a significant cause of vision loss despite the widespread use of anti-VEGF therapy. Nearly half of patients experience suboptimal responses in both anatomical and functional outcomes. This study correlates molecular signatures with clinical outcomes to identify associative markers of early treatment response and optimize DME management. METHODS: Serum samples from 44 DME patients, treated with ≥3 anti-VEGF injections and 6 months follow-up, classified as responders or non-responders. Multiplex bead-based assays were used to measure cytokines related to vascular integrity, inflammatory, and adhesion molecules. Statistical analysis was performed using GraphPad. retina.title: Continuous efficacy and safety of fluocinolone acetonide implant: long-term insights in diabetic macular edema patients from a portuguese hospital.
retina.summary: The 0.19 mg FAc implant was associated with sustained anatomical and functional improvements over 36 months as part of the management of refractory DME. Long-term IOP monitoring remains essential.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the efficacy and safety of the 0.19 mg intravitreal fluocinolone acetonide (FAc) implant over a 36-month period in patients with refractory diabetic macular edema (DME). METHODS: Retrospective, single-center study including patients with refractory DME treated with the FAc implant, with outcomes assessed over 36 months. The primary endpoint was the proportion of eyes with CRT ≤ 280 μm at month 36. RESULTS: Ninety-one eyes from 62 patients were included, with a mean baseline BCVA of 44.7 ± 18.1 ETDRS letters, CRT of 508.6 ± 176.2 μm, and DME duration of 3.6 ± 1.9 years. Eyes had received a median of 6 anti-VEGF injections (IQR, 3-13) and 2 corticosteroid injections (IQR, 1-3), and 23 (25.3%) were phakic. retina.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, with neovascular AMD (nAMD) characterized by choroidal neovascularization (CNV) and subretinal fibrosis. Although anti-VEGF therapy is the current standard, frequent injections and limited efficacy necessitate alternative treatments. The mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway contributes to AMD by promoting oxidative stress-induced apoptosis, inflammation, and angiogenesis. We evaluated the therapeutic potential of MAPK-targeting microRNAs (miRNAs) delivered via recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV). Two rAAV2.7m8-based strategies were developed: a MAPK-miR mixture (three individually packaged miRNAs: hsa-miR-122-5p, let-7a-5p, and miR-26a-5p) and an MAPK-miR tandem (all three miRNAs in one vector under separate U6 promoters). Intravitreal administration of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents has become the standard first-line treatment for nAMD. …
retina.abstract: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is primarily characterized by the formation of abnormal choroidal neovascularization and can lead to substantial visual impairment. Intravitreal administration of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents has become the standard first-line treatment for nAMD. However, challenges remain, including the need for frequent injections, considerable treatment burden, and suboptimal responses in a subset of patients. In recent years, the emergence of high-dose anti-VEGF therapies has provided a novel strategy for extending treatment intervals and optimizing long-term disease management. To address these clinical needs, the Ophthalmology Group of China Alliance for Rare Diseases/Beijing Society of Rare Disease Clinical Care and Accessibility organized a multidisciplinary panel of experts to develop this consensus. retina.summary: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a prevalent potentially blinding retinal vascular disease, with secondary macular edema, retinal ischemia, and ocular neovascular complications posing substantial threats to visual function. …
retina.abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a prevalent potentially blinding retinal vascular disease, with secondary macular edema, retinal ischemia, and ocular neovascular complications posing substantial threats to visual function. Supported by members of the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology (AAPPO), Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society (APVRS) and Academia Retina Internationalis (ARI), a consensus and guideline is provided a comprehensive update on the etiology, diagnosis and management of RVO. An updated consensus was judged necessary following numerous recent results from epidemiology studies, evolution of advanced imaging technologies and novel pharmacotherapeutics from clinical trials, including an expanding portfolio of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents, drug delivery systems, and emerging evidence on relevant artificial intelligence. retina.title: Study Design for ELARA, a Phase 3b Trial of Aflibercept 8 mg in Previously Treated Patients With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration or Diabetic Macular Edema.
retina.summary: INTRODUCTION: Aflibercept 8 mg at extended dosing intervals demonstrated functional and anatomic improvements in a large majority of patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) or diabetic macular edema (DME) in pivotal trials. …
retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aflibercept 8 mg at extended dosing intervals demonstrated functional and anatomic improvements in a large majority of patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) or diabetic macular edema (DME) in pivotal trials. Although a subset of patients may require frequent injections to maintain disease control, the efficacy and safety of monthly dosing with aflibercept 8 mg had not been extensively assessed. The ELARA trial evaluated the tolerability and measures of efficacy of aflibercept 8 mg every 4 weeks, as well as the feasibility of dosing interval extension following 6 monthly doses of aflibercept 8 mg, in previously treated patients with nAMD or DME. METHODS: ELARA was a multicenter, open-label, 96-week, phase 3b trial. retina.title: Clinical exit strategy in anti-VEGF therapy for neovascular AMD: incidence of recurrence and risk factors for relapse.
retina.summary: Recurrence after anti-VEGF discontinuation is common in neovascular AMD. The presence of extrafoveal intraretinal fluid and retinal pigment epithelium tear at treatment cessation may increase the risk of relapse, highlighting the need for cautious treatment exit strategies and close post-discontinuation monitoring.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the recurrence rate of neovascular activity after discontinuation of intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and to identify baseline clinical and imaging factors associated with relapse following a clinical exit strategy. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients with neovascular AMD who discontinued anti-VEGF therapy due to a clinical decision were identified. Treatment discontinuation was based on the absence of foveal exudation on optical coherence tomography (OCT). Baseline demographic, clinical, and OCT characteristics were analyzed. The primary outcome was disease recurrence, defined as the need for a new intravitreal anti-VEGF injection during follow-up. retina.title: Longer-term outcomes of intravitreal therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration at a peripheral centre (Palmerston North eye clinic).
retina.summary: High early cessation due to end-stage disease suggests possible late presentation, underscoring the need for earlier detection and referral. Addressing logistical barriers and supporting adherence will be increasingly important as demand for anti-VEGF therapy grows with an ageing population.
retina.abstract: AIM: The aim of this study was to evaluate long-term real-world outcomes of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) at a regional New Zealand centre, with a primary focus on treatment duration and reasons for cessation. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Palmerston North eye clinic, including all newly diagnosed eyes with nAMD initiating anti-VEGF therapy between November 2017 and August 2023. Demographic data, visual acuity, treatment duration and documented reasons for cessation were extracted from a prospectively maintained database and validated against electronic health records. RESULTS: Among 527 eyes from 446 patients, 39.8% ceased treatment. retina.title: Multicentre Real-World Evaluation of Intravitreal Bevacizumab, Aflibercept, and Ranibizumab for Diabetic Macular Edema.
retina.summary: In this real-world multicenter cohort, VA improved after anti-VEGF treatment, without a significant between-group difference in the primary visual endpoint. Aflibercept (2 mg) was associated with more favorable secondary anatomical and treatment-burden metrics in adjusted analyses. …
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the real-world effectiveness and treatment patterns of intravitreal bevacizumab, aflibercept (2 mg), and ranibizumab in patients newly diagnosed with diabetic macular edema (DME). METHODS: A retrospective, multicenter observational study with a one-year follow-up was conducted at public clinics in Israel and Canada. A total of 309 eyes from 277 treatment-naive patients with DME were analyzed, including both eyes from 32 patients. Eyes were grouped by first-line therapy: bevacizumab (n=199), aflibercept 2 mg (n=63), or ranibizumab (n=47). The primary endpoint was change in visual acuity (VA) at one year. Secondary endpoints included change in central retinal thickness (CRT), injection frequency, final injection interval, and treatment response metrics. retina.title: Five-Year Treatment Outcomes of Macular Oedema Secondary to Central Retinal Vein Occlusion in Routine Clinical Practice: The Fight Retinal Blindness! Registry.
retina.summary: Patients with macular oedema secondary to CRVO who continue treatment can achieve meaningful improvements in vision over an extended period. Patients with initially poor vision tend to have large improvements but the worst outcomes. …
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: To report 5-year outcomes in a cohort of patients who received anti-VEGF therapy for macular oedema secondary to central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) in routine clinical practice. METHODS: In this retrospective observational study, 593 treatment-naïve eyes that commenced anti-VEGF treatment between 1 January 2010, and 2019 were analysed. Outcome measures included mean changes in visual acuity (VA) and central subfield thickness (CST). RESULTS: In the entire cohort (593), the mean VA changed by +8 letters and the mean CST by -298 μm. The entire cohort includes eyes with completed 5-year follow-up and non-completers who dropped out before the end of the observation period. Eyes that completed the 5-year follow-up (202/593, 34%) had a mean VA and CST change of +11 letters and -320 μm with a median of 25.5 injections at 39.5 visits. retina.title: Management of Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Routine US Clinical Practice: Impact of Delayed Treatment Initiation.
retina.summary: Overall, approximately one-quarter of eyes with nAMD were not treated within 29 days of diagnosis. Simultaneous bilateral nAMD diagnosis and poor baseline VA (< 20/400) were primary factors associated with not receiving anti-VEGF treatment. Greater VA gains were observed with prompt treatment and increasing number of injections.
retina.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To understand management of patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) in routine US clinical practice to identify gaps in patient care. DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of electronic medical records from the Vestrum database. PARTICIPANTS: Treatment-naive eyes newly diagnosed with nAMD from January 1, 2014, with ≥1-years' follow-up. METHODS: Cumulative incidence of eyes receiving treatment was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier, and factors predicting anti-VEGF receipt through 1 year were evaluated by logistic regression. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Proportion of eyes treated over 3 years, baseline factors associated with receiving treatment within 1 year of diagnosis and with delayed (3-12 months after diagnosis) versus prompt (within 29 days of diagnosis) treatment initiation. retina.title: Mechanistic Insights into the Combined Anti-inflammatory Effects of Bevacizumab and Triamcinolone in Hyperglycemic Retinal Cells: Modulation of MCP-1, CXCL10, and Their Receptors.
retina.summary: These results reveal that triamcinolone may complement bevacizumab by targeting VEGF-independent inflammatory pathways, providing mechanistic insight into combination therapy for diabetic macular edema (DME), particularly in patients with persistent DME despite anti-VEGF monotherapy.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: Diabetic retinopathy is marked by hyperglycemia-induced inflammation and chemokine signaling that drive immune cell infiltration and retinal damage. As bevacizumab offers limited benefit in some cases, targeting broader inflammatory pathways with agents like triamcinolone may enhance therapeutic outcomes. METHODS: ARPE-19 cells exposed to hyperglycemic conditions (30 mM glucose) for 72 hours were treated with bevacizumab (0.3 mg/ml), triamcinolone (1mg/ml), or their combination. Cell proliferation was assessed using the MTT assay, while ELISA measured VEGF, MCP-1, and CXCL10 secretion, and qRT-PCR analyzed CCR2 and CXCR3 gene expression. retina.title: Intravitreal faricimab in patients with nAMD: French data from the Fight Retinal Blindness! Registry.
retina.summary: Macular neovascularization (MNV) inactivation and modest interval extension were observed in active eyes; inactive eyes showed a larger interval extension. Loading dose was not associated with better outcomes in this observational cohort. Safety was acceptable.
retina.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess real-world outcomes of intravitreal faricimab in French patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) previously treated with vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) inhibitors using data from the Fight Retinal Blindness! (FRB!) Registry. METHODS: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected FRB! Registry data (November 2023-March 2026) on eyes switched to faricimab from other VEGF inhibitors. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: change in injection interval at 12 months. Secondary endpoints: macular neovascularization (MNV) inactivation, visual acuity (VA), injections, switch-off, safety. Mixed-effects models assessed baseline predictors of interval change and loading-dose effect on MNV inactivation. retina.title: Real-world durability of faricimab in treatment-naïve nAMD patients: outcomes of an observe-and-plan regimen.
retina.summary: Faricimab demonstrates strong real-world efficacy, enabling immediate extension of treatment intervals under an O&P regimen. Baseline CRT is an important anatomical biomarker that helps tailor treatment regimens to individuals and reduce treatment burden.
retina.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the long-term durability and treatment-free intervals of treatment-naïve patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) treated with faricimab under an observe-and-plan (O&P) regimen in a real-world setting. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 410 treatment-naïve eyes with active nAMD. All eyes received an initial loading phase consisting of three monthly intravitreal injections of faricimab. RESULT: A total of 1,040 patients were included across 10 articles, where 531 patients had been treated with IVR and 509 with laser photocoagulation. Currently, intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti‑VEGF) injections are the first‑line pharmacological treatment for the management of center‑involving DME. retina.abstract: Studies have identified the involvement of microvascular injury, neurovascular unit (NVU) dysfunction, and retinal hemodynamic abnormalities in diabetic retinal diseases, including diabetic retinopathy and diabetic macular edema (DME). Although chronic hyperglycemia is the central driver of retinal damage, mounting evidence suggests that neuronal dysfunction, glial activation, impaired neurovascular coupling, and altered retinal circulation may occur before the development of clinically visible vascular lesions. These changes may reflect an early mismatch between neuronal metabolic demand and vascular supply, contributing to retinal ischemia and disease progression. retina.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is one of the major complications of diabetes mellitus and a leading cause of visual loss. Diabetic macular edema (DME) is an ocular manifestation of the disease causing visual deterioration. The prevalence of visual impairment due to DME is estimated to be 5.4% in Europe. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is overexpressed in diabetic eyes and plays a key role in the development of DME. VEGF levels were proven to be elevated in the vitreous and retina in patients with diabetic retinopathy. VEGF causes a breakdown of the blood-retinal barrier by influencing the tight junctions of retinal endothelial cells and leading to accumulation of fluid in the macula. Therefore, intravitreal VEGF inhibitors are ideal candidates to treat DME by counteracting VEGF overexpression. Although laser photocoagulation has been the standard treatment of DME for nearly three decades, superior outcomes can be achieved with novel, intravitreal anti-VEGF and steroid therapy. RESULTS: A TER algorithm was developed; TER is defined as an individualized proactive dosing regimen usually initiated by monthly injections until a maximal clinical response is observed (frequently determined by optical coherence tomography), followed by increasing intervals between injections (and evaluations) depending on disease activity. retina.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of severe vision loss in individuals over the age of 50 years. Choroidal neovascularization (CNV) is the hallmark of 'wet' or 'exudative' AMD, and is responsible for approximately 90% of cases of severe vision loss due to AMD. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is a key component in the development and progression of wet AMD. Since the approval of ranibizumab in 2006, VEGF inhibitors have rapidly altered the treatment and standard of care for wet AMD. Ranibizumab, bevacizumab, and aflibercept are now the most widely used anti-VEGF agents for the treatment of wet AMD. retina.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration is the most common cause of vision loss in elderly people in developed countries. Nowadays, in clinical practice, three anti-VEGF drugs are commonly used (bevacizumab, aflibercept and ranibizumab), requiring repeated intravitreal injections. In order to minimise the number of injections, research on intravitreal drug delivery systems (DDSs) is needed. In this review, the DDSs developed up to date regarding intravitreal anti-VEGF drugs have been summarised, which include systems as hydrogels, liposomes, microparticles, nanoparticles or implants. retina.abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is the second most common cause of visual loss in the Western World. RVO is usually classified into branch RVO (BRVO) and central RVO (CRVO) according to the anatomical site of the vascular occlusion. The blockage of venous circulation causes an elevation of intraluminal pressure in the capillaries, leading to hemorrhages and leakage of fluid within the retina, increase of interstitial pressure and a consequent reduction of retinal perfusion. We also discuss the advantages and disadvantages of both regimens, as well as monitoring and treatment of the disease, including treatment intervals and injection frequency. retina.abstract: INTRODUCTION: In developed countries, neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of irreversible central blindness. Although AMD pathogenesis is complex and still not fully understood, many involved mechanisms are already partially known and could be promising targets for future therapies. Currently, anti-VEGF drugs are the standard care of this condition. AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes both the current available and the emerging pharmacological therapies for the management of neovascular AMD. At first, we briefly focused on anti-VEGF compounds that are commonly used. Then, we reviewed the mechanisms of action and potential advantages of new candidate drugs that are being evaluated in clinical trials. retina.abstract: Since their introduction in the late 2000s, anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) agents have become the first-line choice for center-involved diabetic macular edema (DME). Even with its proven effectiveness, there are still cases that do not respond satisfactorily. In those cases, a treatment option is to change to another anti-VEGF drug. In this paper, the authors review studies on switching between different anti-VEGF drugs in the treatment of persistent DME. An extensive bibliographic review was done using PubMed, Embase, and Scopus. Fourteen studies published from March 2010 to April 2017 reporting switching from anti-VEGF drugs in DME treatment were included. retina.abstract: The issue of macular retinal degeneration is one of the key areas of ophthalmology. Recent advances in the targeted delivery of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) suppressants have significantly impacted the patient's prognosis in the form of a significant deceleration in disease progression. Some of the drugs have gradually found their use in other indications (central retinal vein occlusion or diabetic macular edema). The following text gives a brief look at the physiology of VEGF, but not only in the eye, but throughout the human body, particularly in the context of adverse effects resulting from systemic inhibition of its effects.

retina.abstract: As the diabetes epidemic in the United States continues to worsen, so too does the prevalence of diabetic retinopathy (DR). DR is divided broadly into nonproliferative and proliferative stages, with or without vision-threatening macular edema. Progression to proliferative DR is associated with vision loss that is often irreparable, and a rapid decline in health-related quality of life. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A is upregulated in the diabetic eye, and has been identified as a key driver of DR pathogenesis. With this perspective, we review the published phase III clinical trial data of anti-VEGF therapies approved for the treatment of DR in the United States. retina.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is referred to as the leading cause of irreversible visual loss in developed countries, with a profound effect on the quality of life. The neovascular form of AMD is characterized by the formation of subretinal choroidal neovascularization, leading to sudden and severe visual loss. Research has identified the vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) as an important pathophysiological component in neovascular AMD and its intraocular inhibition as one of the most efficient therapies in medicine. The introduction of anti-VEGF as a standard treatment in wet AMD has led to a great improvement in the prognosis of patients, allowing recovery and maintenance of visual function in the vast majority of cases. retina.title: Anti-VEGF Molecules for the Management of Diabetic Macular Edema.
retina.summary: Diabetic macular edema (DME) represents the most common cause of vision loss in patients affected by diabetes mellitus. Although the pathophysiology of DME is not wholly understood, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) has been identified as a key contributor to the development of DME. …
retina.abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME) represents the most common cause of vision loss in patients affected by diabetes mellitus. Although the pathophysiology of DME is not wholly understood, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) has been identified as a key contributor to the development of DME. In addition, latest information suggests that acute and chronic inflammatory changes occur, contributing to the DME pathogenesis. The current therapeutic approach for DME is mainly based on the administration of anti-VEGF molecules. In particular, VEGF-inhibitors that have been studied for diabetic retinopathy include pegaptanib, ranibizumab, bevacizumab, and aflibercept. The present review analyzes the main characteristics of each molecule, describing the most important results of clinical trails.

retina.abstract: Approximately 40% of patients with diabetic macular edema (DME) are resistant to anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy (rDME). Here, we demonstrate that significant correlations between inflammatory cytokines and VEGF, as observed in naive DME, are lost in patients with rDME. Phosphorylated protein analysis of VEGF-overexpressed retinas revealed rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase (ROCK) activation. retina.title: Identifying Genetic Risk Factors for Diabetic Macular Edema and the Response to Treatment.
retina.summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). DR is complex and the term encompasses several clinical subtypes of diabetic eye disease, including diabetic macular edema (DME), the most frequent cause of central vision loss in DR patients. …
retina.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). DR is complex and the term encompasses several clinical subtypes of diabetic eye disease, including diabetic macular edema (DME), the most frequent cause of central vision loss in DR patients. Both genetic and environmental factors contribute to the pathophysiology of DR and its subtypes. While numerous studies have identified several susceptibility genes for DR, few have investigated the impact of genetics on DME susceptibility. This review will focus on the current literature surrounding genetic risk factors associated with DME. We will also highlight the small number of studies investigating the genetics of response to antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injection, which is used to treat DME.

retina.abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME), defined as a retinal thickening involving or approaching the center of the macula, represents the most common cause of vision loss in patients affected by diabetes mellitus. In the last few years, many diagnostic tools have been proven useful in the detection and the monitoring of the features characterizing DME. On the other hand, several therapeutic approaches can now be proposed on the basis of the DME-specific characteristics. The aim of the present chapter is to thoroughly delineate the clinical and morpho functional characteristics of DME and its current treatment perspectives. The pathogenesis and the course of DME require a complex approach with multidisciplinary intervention both at the systemic and local levels.

retina.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF-A) is a key cytokine in the development of normal blood vessels as well as the development of vessels in tumors and other tissues undergoing abnormal angiogenesis. Here, we review the molecular engineering of two humanized antibodies derived from a common mouse anti-VEGF antibody--bevacizumab, a full-length IgG1 approved for the treatment of specified cancer indications, and ranibizumab, an affinity-matured antibody Fab domain approved for use in age-related macular degeneration (AMD). In clinical trials and as FDA-approved therapeutics, these two anti-VEGF antibodies, bevacizumab (Avastin anti-VEGF antibody) and ranibizumab (Lucentis anti-VEGF antibody), have demonstrated therapeutic utility in blocking VEGF-induced angiogenesis.

As the usually small fibrovascular lesions show a rapid progression in the spontaneous course of the disease and lead to irreversible damage to the photoreceptors, prompt initiation of treatment is mandatory. retina.abstract: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a visually devastating condition resulting from choroidal neovascularization and secondary photoreceptor loss. Ranibizumab and bevacizumab are medications that target vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). While other therapies have demonstrated some ability to reduce the risk of losing vision from neovascular AMD, most patients continue to lose some degree of central visual acuity. There is growing evidence that intravitreal administration of ranibizumab and bevacizumab is effective in significantly improving the visual acuity in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

We reviewed the current literature on this topic: case reports, non controlled and non randomized trials. retina.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A is a major regulator of angiogenesis and vascular permeability implicated in the development of diseases involving pathological angiogenesis and increased vascular permeability, such as neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD). LUCENTIS (ranibizumab), a humanized antigen-binding fragment (Fab) that neutralizes all VEGF-A isoforms and their biologically active degradation products, was recently approved by the FDA. Ranibizumab is the first FDA-approved treatment for neovascular AMD that maintains or improves vision in > or = 90% patients and provides a > or = 15-letter improvement in visual acuity for a quarter to a third of patients with all choroidal neovascularisation subtypes. retina.abstract: Blood vessels deliver oxygen and nutrients to every part of the body, but also nourish diseases such as cancer. Over the past decade, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms of angiogenesis (blood vessel growth) has increased at an explosive rate and has led to the approval of anti-angiogenic drugs for cancer and eye diseases. So far, hundreds of thousands of patients have benefited from blockers of the angiogenic protein vascular endothelial growth factor, but limited efficacy and resistance remain outstanding problems. Recent preclinical and clinical studies have shown new molecular targets and principles, which may provide avenues for improving the therapeutic benefit from anti-angiogenic strategies.

retina.abstract: Fibrosis is defined by the overgrowth, hardening, and/or scarring of various tissues and is attributed to excess deposition of extracellular matrix components including collagen. Fibrosis is the end result of chronic inflammatory reactions induced by a variety of stimuli including persistent infections, autoimmune reactions, allergic responses, chemical insults, radiation, and tissue injury. Although current treatments for fibrotic diseases such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, liver cirrhosis, systemic sclerosis, progressive kidney disease, and cardiovascular fibrosis typically target the inflammatory response, there is accumulating evidence that the mechanisms driving fibrogenesis are distinct from those regulating inflammation. retina.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is an endothelial cell-specific mitogen in vitro and an angiogenic inducer in a variety of in vivo models. Hypoxia has been shown to be a major inducer of VEGF gene transcription. The tyrosine kinases Flt-1 (VEGFR-1) and Flk-1/KDR (VEGFR-2) are high-affinity VEGF receptors. The role of VEGF in developmental angiogenesis is emphasized by the finding that loss of a single VEGF allele results in defective vascularization and early embryonic lethality. VEGF is critical also for reproductive and bone angiogenesis. Substantial evidence also implicates VEGF as a mediator of pathological angiogenesis. In situ hybridization studies demonstrate expression of VEGF mRNA in the majority of human tumors. retina.abstract: In 2008, we published the first set of guidelines for standardizing research in autophagy. Since then, this topic has received increasing attention, and many scientists have entered the field. Our knowledge base and relevant new technologies have also been expanding. Thus, it is important to formulate on a regular basis updated guidelines for monitoring autophagy in different organisms. Despite numerous reviews, there continues to be confusion regarding acceptable methods to evaluate autophagy, especially in multicellular eukaryotes. Here, we present a set of guidelines for investigators to select and interpret methods to examine autophagy and related processes, and for reviewers to provide realistic and reasonable critiques of reports that are focused on these processes. retina.summary: In the 10 years that have passed since the Nobel prize-winning discovery of RNA interference (RNAi), billions of dollars have been invested in the therapeutic application of gene silencing in humans. …
retina.abstract: In the 10 years that have passed since the Nobel prize-winning discovery of RNA interference (RNAi), billions of dollars have been invested in the therapeutic application of gene silencing in humans. Today, there are promising data from ongoing clinical trials for the treatment of age-related macular degeneration and respiratory syncytial virus. Despite these early successes, however, the widespread use of RNAi therapeutics for disease prevention and treatment requires the development of clinically suitable, safe and effective drug delivery vehicles. Here, we provide an update on the progress of RNAi therapeutics and highlight novel synthetic materials for the encapsulation and intracellular delivery of nucleic acids.

retina.abstract: The multifunctional regulator nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor (Nrf2) is considered not only as a cytoprotective factor regulating the expression of genes coding for anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory and detoxifying proteins, but it is also a powerful modulator of species longevity. The vertebrate Nrf2 belongs to Cap 'n' Collar (Cnc) bZIP family of transcription factors and shares a high homology with SKN-1 from Caenorhabditis elegans or CncC found in Drosophila melanogaster. The major characteristics of Nrf2 are to some extent mimicked by Nrf2-dependent genes and their proteins including heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1), which besides removing toxic heme, produces biliverdin, iron ions and carbon monoxide. retina.title: Resolving inflammation: dual anti-inflammatory and pro-resolution lipid mediators
retina.summary: Active resolution of acute inflammation is a previously unrecognized interface between innate and adaptive immunity. Once thought to be a passive process, the resolution of inflammation is now shown to involve active biochemical programmes that enable inflamed tissues to return to homeostasis. …
retina.abstract: Active resolution of acute inflammation is a previously unrecognized interface between innate and adaptive immunity. Once thought to be a passive process, the resolution of inflammation is now shown to involve active biochemical programmes that enable inflamed tissues to return to homeostasis. This Review presents new cellular and molecular mechanisms for the resolution of inflammation, revealing key roles for eicosanoids, such as lipoxins, and recently discovered families of endogenous chemical mediators, termed resolvins and protectins. These mediators have anti-inflammatory and pro-resolution properties, thereby protecting organs from collateral damage, stimulating the clearance of inflammatory debris and promoting mucosal antimicrobial defence.

retina.abstract: The discovery of vascular endothelial-derived growth factor (VEGF) has revolutionized our understanding of vasculogenesis and angiogenesis during development and physiological homeostasis. Over a short span of two decades, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which VEGF coordinates neurovascular homeostasis has become more sophisticated. The central role of VEGF in the pathogenesis of diverse cancers and blinding eye diseases has also become evident. Elucidation of the molecular regulation of VEGF and the transformative development of multiple therapeutic pathways targeting VEGF directly or indirectly is a powerful case study of how fundamental research can guide innovation and translation. Recent advances in developing clinically desirable AAV capsids, optimizing genome designs and harnessing revolutionary biotechnologies have contributed substantially to the growth of the gene therapy field. …
retina.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors are the leading platform for gene delivery for the treatment of a variety of human diseases. Recent advances in developing clinically desirable AAV capsids, optimizing genome designs and harnessing revolutionary biotechnologies have contributed substantially to the growth of the gene therapy field. Preclinical and clinical successes in AAV-mediated gene replacement, gene silencing and gene editing have helped AAV gain popularity as the ideal therapeutic vector, with two AAV-based therapeutics gaining regulatory approval in Europe or the United States. Continued study of AAV biology and increased understanding of the associated therapeutic challenges and limitations will build the foundation for future clinical success.

dryeye.abstract: ROS-related ophthalmic diseases span the ocular surface as well as the anterior and posterior segments of the eye. Dry eye disease (DED), glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy (DR) and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) have distinct anatomical targets but share common pathophysiological features, including oxidative stress, inflammation, vascular dysfunction, epithelial injury or neurodegeneration. Conventional ocular drug delivery and therapeutic modalities are hindered by severe limitations, including low bioavailability in the posterior segment of the eye and the requirement for frequent invasive administration. METHODS: This cross-sectional reanalysis used a retrospective, de-identified dataset collected in Gaza in 2023. dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a chronic, multifactorial inflammatory disorder characterized by tear film instability, epithelial damage, and neurosensory abnormalities that compromise ocular surface (OS) homeostasis. Oxidative stress, immune dysregulation and metabolic imbalance contribute to epithelial damage and inflammation. Emerging evidence highlights nutrition as a modifiable adjunctive factor in DED management. dryeye.abstract: Reduced tear output can arise from altered neural regulation, impaired epithelial secretion, or loss of secretory tissue, with different implications for recovery. This focused narrative review integrates physiological, single-cell, spatial, organoid, and mechanistic studies identified through a structured PubMed search and targeted reference checking. We examine how remodeling of the lacrimal secretory niche affects acinar secretory competence, the capacity of viable acinar cells to convert stimulation into coordinated fluid, electrolyte, and protein secretion. Omics studies identify disease-associated expression patterns and candidate interactions, while selected perturbation studies link neural, inflammatory, and metabolic mechanisms to secretory dysfunction. dryeye.title: Vision-Related Quality of Life and Dry Eye Symptoms After Treatment with Lyophilized Amniotic Membrane Eye Drops: A Secondary Analysis of a Prospective Cohort Study.
dryeye.summary: Background/Objectives: Dry eye disease (DED) affects daily visual functioning and vision-related quality of life in addition to tear film stability and ocular surface integrity. …
dryeye.abstract: Background/Objectives: Dry eye disease (DED) affects daily visual functioning and vision-related quality of life in addition to tear film stability and ocular surface integrity. In a previously published prospective cohort, lyophilized amniotic membrane (AM) eye drops were associated with significant improvements in objective ocular surface parameters. This secondary analysis evaluated whether treatment with lyophilized AM eye drops was accompanied by changes in patient-reported outcomes, specifically vision-related quality of life and dry eye symptoms. Methods: This secondary analysis included 40 consecutive patients with DED treated with lyophilized AM eye drops in repeated 14-day cycles over six study visits, while continuing their pre-existing standard DED therapy. dryeye.abstract: Background: This study evaluated the efficacy of topical azithromycin ophthalmic solution (Azyter®, 15 mg/g) as second-line treatment for mixed dry eye disease (DED), given the drug's known non-antimicrobial anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties. Methods: In this pilot, prospective, controlled, non-randomized interventional study, fifteen patients with mixed DED refractory to first-line treatment received topical azithromycin for 30 days (twice daily for 3 days, then once daily for 27 days); ten healthy individuals served as controls. Clinical evaluation was performed before and after treatment in the study group and once in controls, and included the Dry Eye Questionnaire-5 (DEQ-5), Schirmer test, non-invasive tear break-up time (NITBUT, Sirius PLUS corneal topography), tear meniscus height (TMH; Sirius PLUS corneal topography), Efron scale grading of blepharitis, meibomian

dryeye.title: Ocular Immune Toxicity in Cancer Immunotherapy, From Immune Privilege Breakdown to Treatment Rechallenge: A Review.
dryeye.summary: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but can disrupt ocular immune privilege and produce heterogeneous immune-related adverse events (Eye-irAEs). …
dryeye.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but can disrupt ocular immune privilege and produce heterogeneous immune-related adverse events (Eye-irAEs). This structured narrative review with evidence mapping integrates clinical, epidemiologic, mechanistic, pharmacovigilance, and management data to define translational pathways from checkpoint blockade to ocular toxicity and treatment decisions. In a real-world cohort of 41,020 ICI-treated patients, ophthalmic irAEs occurred in 4.18% within 1 year, including dry eye disease in 2.00%, conjunctivitis in 0.87%, blepharitis in 0.51%, anterior uveitis in 0.39%, and keratitis in 0.38%. dryeye.title: Determining value and the contribution of ciclosporin-based therapies in dry eye disease: a European expert MCDA pilot study.
dryeye.summary: The expert opinion, based on MCDA, enabled the identification of key value drivers and unmet needs in the current management of DED based on ciclosporin-based therapies. These early insights may contribute to promoting future work to support informed, evidence-based decision-making.
dryeye.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dry eye disease (DED) is a multifactorial, immune-mediated inflammatory condition affecting the ocular surface and lacrimal glands. Multiple ciclosporin-based therapies with different formulations are currently available in Europe, although clear guidance on their optimal use remains limited. The aim of this study was to determine the main unmet needs and the current management landscape of ciclosporin-based therapies, from the perspective of clinical experts using multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA). METHODS: A systematic literature review was conducted to gather evidence for each of the MCDA framework criteria. An international expert panel of seven clinical specialists in DED from four European countries independently weighted the criteria and scored the non-comparative criteria in the evidence matrix. Results were presented and discussed in a group online session. R

dryeye.abstract: Ocular drug delivery is severely affected by anatomical and physiological ocular barriers, preventing drug permeation and therapeutic effects. Uveitis, keratitis, and inflammatory postoperative ocular complications demand accurate, sustained, and localized therapy. Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs) and Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs (Corticosteroids) are cornerstones for managing anterior and posterior ocular inflammation. Their traditional formulations, however, are flawed, with compromised bioavailability, tear clearance, and systemic toxicity. Nano-formulations prepared using the latest breakthroughs in nanotechnology have transformed ophthalmic drug delivery by offering enhanced solubility, prolonged retention time, and extended drug release. dryeye.title: Emerging RNA-Based Therapeutic Strategies for Inflammatory Ophthalmic Disorders of the Anterior Segment: Mechanistic Insights and Translational Potential.
dryeye.summary: Anterior segment ocular inflammatory disorders, including conjunctivitis, keratitis, scleritis, dry eye disease, and anterior uveitis, represent a major cause of visual impairment worldwide. …
dryeye.abstract: Anterior segment ocular inflammatory disorders, including conjunctivitis, keratitis, scleritis, dry eye disease, and anterior uveitis, represent a major cause of visual impairment worldwide. Conventional pharmacological therapies such as antihistamines, corticosteroids, and immunomodulators primarily provide symptomatic relief but are limited by their adverse effects, poor long-term efficacy, and lack of disease-modifying potential. In this review, RNA-based therapeutics are discussed in detail, emerging as promising and targeted approaches for modulating the molecular mechanisms underlying ocular anterior segment inflammatory conditions. These strategies include small interfering RNA (siRNA), short hairpin RNA (shRNA), antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), messenger RNA (mRNA), microRNA (miRNA), and long noncoding RNA (lncRNA), each offering distinct mechanisms to regulate gene expression

dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term ocular surface outcomes after upper-eyelid-sparing management of large lower-eyelid defects. METHODS: Twelve patients with large lower-eyelid defects after tumor excision were managed without surgical involvement of the upper eyelid using either laissez-faire (secondary intention, n = 11) healing or primary closure under tension (n = 1). The operated eye was compared with the contralateral, non-operated eye. Assessments included the Dry Eye Questionnaire-5 (DEQ-5), margin- reflex distance (MRD) 1 and 2, tear break-up time (TBUT), tear meniscus height (TMH), ocular staining score (OSS), and infrared meibography. dryeye.title: Heavy-metal exposure and ocular diseases: A systematic review integrating exposure biomarkers and mechanistic insights.
dryeye.summary: Heavy metals, including lead, cadmium, mercury, and arsenic, are persistent environmental contaminants whose accumulation in ocular tissues represents an underrecognized pathway to visual impairment. …
dryeye.abstract: Heavy metals, including lead, cadmium, mercury, and arsenic, are persistent environmental contaminants whose accumulation in ocular tissues represents an underrecognized pathway to visual impairment. This systematic review synthesizes evidence from 2015 to 2026 on the sources, transport, fate, and toxicological effects of heavy metals in the ocular environment. Epidemiological studies suggest associations between chronic exposure and a spectrum of ocular pathologies, including dry eye syndrome, glaucoma, cataract, age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, and toxic optic neuropathy. Following environmental release, metals enter the eye through two primary pathways: direct deposition onto the ocular surface from contaminated air, and systemic translocation across blood-ocular barriers. dryeye.title: USB-powered vs. self-heating warm compresses for meibomian gland dysfunction: A prospective randomized crossover clinical trial.
dryeye.summary: USB-powered warm compresses provided superior outcomes in enhancing tear film stability and volume compared to self-heating masks. Consistent temperature control and reusability make them a promising at-home therapy for patients with MGD. …
dryeye.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dry eye syndrome (DES) is a prevalent multifactorial condition characterized by tear film instability and meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD). Warm compress therapy remains a cornerstone for improving lipid layer function. However, very limited comparative data exist on newer USB-powered devices vs. self-heating masks in Middle Eastern populations. METHODS: This randomized crossover clinical trial compared USB-powered and self-heating masks in 15 participants aged 18-40 years with meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD) associated eye (tear break-up time ≤10 s). Each intervention was scheduled for five consecutive days, separated by a two-week washout. METHOD: We systematically reviewed 127 studies (2013-2023; 368 datasets). …
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the effect of anti-inflammatory drug classes, delivery methods, and personalized regimens on ocular surface health in dry eye patients, providing evidence-based support for optimizing medication regimens. METHOD: We systematically reviewed 127 studies (2013-2023; 368 datasets). Multiple linear regression analyzed tear film breakup time (TBUT) predictors. dryeye.summary: These results suggest that topical insulin drops are a safe and affordable treatment option for ocular surface diseases, particularly for NK eyes with and without PED. Further prospective clinical trials, however, are needed to confirm the efficacy and define the place of topical insulin in standardized treatment protocols.
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the efficacy of topical insulin for the treatment of various ocular surface diseases. METHODS: A retrospective, multicenter cohort study was conducted at the university hospitals of Brussels and Ghent and included 57 eyes (45 patients) treated with topical insulin (1 IU/mL 4 times daily) for neurotrophic keratopathy (NK) (n = 31), dry eye disease (DED) (n = 9), graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) (n = 7), and various other ocular surface diseases (n = 10) between October 2023 and March 2025. Data from medical records and anterior segment photographs were analyzed. Primary outcome was treatment success; secondary outcomes included clinical evolution, symptoms, data on persistent epithelial defects (PED), vision, and adverse events. dryeye.title: The Meibomian Gland Composite Score (MGCS): A Novel Grading System Integrating Existing Scales for Meibomian Gland Dysfunction.
dryeye.summary: The MGCS offers a standardized and continuous scale for assessing MGD severity. By incorporating detailed meibum texture descriptions supported by standardized pictorial and video references, the scale facilitates precise disease tracking and robust statistical analysis in both clinical practice and research settings.
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To introduce and evaluate the clinical performance of the Meibomian Gland Composite Score (MGCS), a novel, standardized, video- and pictorial-based grading system designed to provide a linear, gland-specific assessment of meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD) severity. METHODS: The MGCS evaluates meibum quality on a 0 to 4 scale based on texture and expressibility across the central 8 upper eyelid glands (score 0-32) and central 5 lower eyelid glands (score 0-20). To evaluate clinical performance, two independent providers performed a retrospective chart review of 53 patients (mean age 60.9 ± 16.4 years; 75.5% female). Th17/Treg imbalance contributes to sustained inflammatory activation in the ocular surface and lacrimal gland. Yiguanjian (YGJ) has anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory potential, but whether it can alleviate ocular surface inflammation and restore lacrimal gland immune homeostasis in DED remains unclear. METHODS: A benzalkonium chloride (BAC)-induced rat DED model was used to assess the effects of YGJ on tear secretion, tear film break-up time, corneal fluorescein staining, ocular histopathology, lacrimal gland Th17/Treg proportions, related gene expression, and STAT3 signaling. dryeye.title: The FAST Study: Examining Quality of Vision Outcomes in Dry Eye Disease Patients with Severe Keratitis Treated with the Ciclosporin A Cationic Emulsion.
dryeye.summary: DED patients with severe keratitis treated with CsA 0.1% CE demonstrated reductions in CFS score that were strongly and significantly correlated with improvements in quality of vision indicators, including VMR and LogMAR FVA. CsA 0.1% CE was well tolerated throughout the study period.
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: Examination of the relationship between improvements in dry eye disease (DED) signs and changes in functional visual acuity (FVA) parameters with ciclosporin A 0.1% cationic emulsion (CsA 0.1% CE) treatment. METHODS: Adults with DED and severe keratitis were included in a Phase IV, prospective, open-label, multicenter, single-arm, proof-of-concept study. Patients instilled CsA 0.1% CE (one drop daily) and unpreserved artificial tears from baseline through month 3. Primary endpoints examined the change from baseline in corneal fluorescein staining (CFS) score (modified Oxford scale) and any correlation with changes in visual maintenance ratio (VMR) or objective scatter index (OSI) variance. dryeye.title: Effects of exogenous relaxin on dry eye in an experimental Sjögren's disease (SS) mouse model.
dryeye.summary: Exogenous relaxin shows therapeutic potential for DED in SS, demonstrated by clinical improvements and reduced inflammatory markers in an animal model of SS.
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the potential of exogenous relaxin (RLX) as a treatment for dry eye disease (DED) in an experimental animal model of Sjögren's disease (SS). METHODS: Nonobese diabetic female (NOD) mice with SS-associated DED received RLX-based or vehicle eye drops (100 ng/mL) four times daily for 30 days. Clinical evaluations included measurements of tear production, assessment of keratitis, and histological analysis of the exorbital lacrimal gland. Inflammatory cytokine expression was measured using PCR. RESULTS: RLX-treated mice showed significant improvement in tear production and keratitis reversal. Qualitative histological analysis suggested better preservation of lacrimal gland architecture, with more evident acinar and ductal structures in the RLX-treated group. dryeye.title: Modified Danzhi Xiaoyao San ameliorates depression-associated dry eye by modulating sphingolipid metabolism across the liver, hippocampus, and lacrimal gland.
dryeye.summary: MDZXYS improved inflammatory, behavioral, and ocular abnormalities and was associated with tissue-specific changes in sphingolipid metabolism across the hippocampus, liver, and lacrimal gland. …

It is traditionally used to soothe the liver, relieve depression, and clear stagnant heat associated with liver-qi stagnation transforming into fire. Grounded in the theory that "the liver opens into the eyes," liver-soothing and heat-clearing strategy has long been applied to treat ocular diseases. Previous studies have reported beneficial effects of Danzhi Xiaoyao San and related modified formulas on depression and dry eye; however, the metabolic basis of their effects across multiple tissues remains incompletely understood. dryeye.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED), a chronic disorder affecting nearly half the global population, is perpetuated by oxidative stress, inflammation, and tear film instability. Constrained by short precorneal residence and monotherapy, DED therapies necessitate frequent dosing and polypharmacy, leaving unmet needs for prolonged ocular retention and multimodal intervention. Herein, we develop berberine (BBR)-loaded dual-dynamically crosslinked nanogels (BBR@MPN-NGs) integrating tannic acid (TA)-zinc metal-polyphenol networks with carboxymethyl chitosan/aldehyde-functionalized poly(ethylene glycol) Schiff base networks, enabling a single-platform multimodal therapy combining antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and lubricating capacities. dryeye.title: Serum Eye Drops for Ocular Surface Disease in Veterinary Ophthalmology: A Translational Review of Human and Veterinary Evidence.
dryeye.summary: SEDs offer physiologically rational adjunctive therapy for OSD in animals. Although serum and plasma have similar antiprotease activity, serum may promote better epithelial healing. Further veterinary studies are warranted.
dryeye.abstract: BACKGROUND: Serum closely resembles natural tears in composition and contains higher growth factor levels than plasma in humans. Beyond its well-established anticollagenase properties, evidence from human ophthalmology suggests a broader therapeutic potential that may extend to the management of ocular surface diseases in animals. OBJECTIVES: This review examines the composition, mechanisms, and clinical applications of serum eye drops (SEDs) in human and veterinary ophthalmology, compares serum with plasma, and proposes a protocol for their formulation. RESULTS: SEDs provide a physiological blend of epitheliotropic factors, including EGF, TGF-β, vitamin A, fibronectin, and protease inhibitors (α2-macroglobulin). dryeye.title: Low-level light therapy for dry eye disease and meibomian gland dysfunction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
dryeye.summary: A healthy tear film is vital for ocular surface integrity and relies on the coordinated function of the lacrimal glands, meibomian glands and conjunctival goblet cells. Dysfunction in any of these elements can lead to dry eye disease (DED). …
dryeye.abstract: A healthy tear film is vital for ocular surface integrity and relies on the coordinated function of the lacrimal glands, meibomian glands and conjunctival goblet cells. Dysfunction in any of these elements can lead to dry eye disease (DED). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of low-level light therapy (LLLT) as a standalone DED treatment. Although evidence for LLLT's therapeutic potential is growing, prior reviews have focused on short-term outcomes or combined LLLT with intense pulsed light. This meta-analysis consolidates current findings to clarify the clinical value of LLLT monotherapy in DED management. We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for studies evaluating LLLT for DED. Study selection and data extraction were conducted according to pre-specified inclusion and exclusion criteria.

dryeye.title: Clinical features and management of medication-induced persistent corneal epithelial defects due to topical ophthalmic medications.
dryeye.summary: The severity of MI-PCED is heavily dependent on the type, subacute duration, and frequency of topical ophthalmic drug use. Management requires a flexible, step-wise strategy focused on restoring ocular surface homeostasis. …
dryeye.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the impact of subacute preservative-containing eye drop usage on the ocular surface and to observe the clinical progression and management of medication-induced persistent corneal epithelial defects (MI-PCED). METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated 60 cases (60 eyes) diagnosed with MI-PCED from January 2020 to January 2024. Data on the type, frequency, and duration of topical medication usage were collected. A multidisciplinary pharmacovigilance assessment evaluated causality, severity, and preventability of the adverse events. Upon diagnosis, the offending medications were discontinued and replaced with low-toxicity, preservative-free alternatives. dryeye.summary: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), as a novel class of targeted anticancer therapies, have demonstrated significantly enhanced efficacy. However, the associated ocular adverse events have emerged as a critical issue impacting patients' quality of life and treatment compliance. …
dryeye.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), as a novel class of targeted anticancer therapies, have demonstrated significantly enhanced efficacy. However, the associated ocular adverse events have emerged as a critical issue impacting patients' quality of life and treatment compliance. ADC-induced ocular adverse events primarily affect corneal and ocular surface tissues. With the recent approval of multiple ADC agents in China and the extensive ongoing clinical trials, standardized guidance for managing corneal and ocular surface adverse events is urgently needed. dryeye.title: Infraorbital Skin Application of Menthol Emulsion for Dry Eye Disease: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
dryeye.summary: In the available analysis population, infraorbital 2% and 4% menthol produced clinically measurable short-latency increases in Schirmer values and tear meniscus height compared with vehicle, supporting further investigation of infraorbital stimulation of endogenous aqueous tear secretion without intentional ocular-surface instillation. …
dryeye.abstract: INTRODUCTION: We aim to evaluate the short-latency tear-secretory effects and symptom responses of infraorbital menthol emulsion in dry eye disease (DED) without intentional ocular-surface instillation. METHODS: In this randomized, participant- and assessor-masked, vehicle-controlled trial, 128 adults with DED were assigned to bilateral infraorbital application of vehicle (0% menthol), 2% menthol, or 4% menthol emulsion four times daily for 3 weeks. Follow-up measurements were obtained 10 min after supervised application. The available analysis population comprised 95 participants (32, 32, and 31, respectively), and efficacy analyses used the right eye. dryeye.abstract: Sjögren disease (SjD) is an autoimmune disease driven by autoimmune CD4+T cells that leads to an immune-mediated loss of lacrimal glands (LG). Meibomian glands are lipid-producing glands in the eyelids that help prevent tear evaporation. While the role of T cells in LG-mediated destruction is well established, it is unknown whether pathogenic T cells can cause MG dysfunction (MGD). Herein, we investigated whether autoimmune CD4+T cells induce MGD and characterized the pathophysiologic mechanisms using an adoptive transfer model. T cells were isolated from CD25KO (KOCD4) or wild-type (WTCD4) mice and transferred into Rag1KO mice. In comparison, KO cells were co-adoptively transferred with WT regulatory T cells (KOCD4 + WTTregs). dryeye.summary: PRP and AS may be more effective than stem cells and cyclosporine A for moderate-to-severe dry eye, but their advantages differ by outcome. PRP may be preferred for symptom relief and tear secretion, whereas AS may better improve tear film stability and corneal staining. …
dryeye.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy of regenerative therapies and conventional anti-inflammatory treatments for moderate-to-severe dry eye and provide evidence for clinical decision-making. METHODS: PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase were systematically searched. Only randomized controlled trials were included. A network meta-analysis compared platelet-rich plasma (PRP), autologous serum (AS), stem cells, 0.05% cyclosporine A, and 0.1% cyclosporine A using OSDI, NIKBUT first, CFS, and Schirmer test outcomes.
